Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: 47: And it is said: "And now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever" (Bereishis 3:22); and they stated [in Bereishis Rabbah 21:6] that He opened for him an entrance to repentance, etc., and "lest" (pen) means "no"—the Holy One, blessed be He, said: shall he put forth, etc., see there.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 41:8
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And even though the covenant was forged over the good destined for the end, nonetheless it is written regarding it “have I given” (in the past tense), since Hashem promised to give it to him, and the utterance of the Holy One is reckoned as though already given, as brought in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 44:22) and as brought in the Talmud (Pesachim 117b): that in the Shema blessing it is 'redeemed Israel' (past), while in the Amidah prayer it is 'Redeems Israel' (present).

English_Source_Translation_And_Context: Zohar, Eikev 1:12-2:20: “In the Zohar (Eikev, Ra’aya Meheimna III 271b), the verse ‘Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled’ (Proverbs 9:5) is expounded as the spiritual nourishment of the soul: ‘bread’ is the Written Torah and ‘wine’ is the esoteric wisdom of the Oral Torah.” Context and connection to Peri Tzadik: In Peri Tzadik, Bereshit 8, Rav Tzadok cites this kabbalistic teaching (Zohar, Eikev 1:12-2:20) to illuminate his exposition here (“as written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 271b). However, once he ate of the tree of knowledge, meaning that he experienced bodily gratification within eating, through this an intermingling was wrought,”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the inner dimensions of Torah and divine service developed in Peri Tzadik.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: Yet there it is not because a father merits for a son, for Scripture precisely addresses "your youth," "your bridal days," "your following Me," viewing the present generation as the very same collective soul that walked through the desert, because Knesset Yisrael is an enduring singular entity across all eras.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 53:1
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “And as for you, you shall keep My covenant” (Genesis 17:9). This verse alludes to active spiritual service from man's initiative: if he desires to comprehend within his intellect to recognize why Hashem chose him to bind with him in a covenant, then he requires active toil to observe Hashem's commandments; wherefore this mitzvah is titled in the holy Zohar (Vayeira 98b) “the tent door”, pointing to this conscious realization, knowing within his soul why Hashem chose him.

English_Source_Translation_And_Context: Tikkunei Zohar 69a:3-70a:3: “In Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 24, 69b–70a), the dispute of the Sages over whether the Tree of Knowledge was wheat, grapes, or figs is explained kabbalistically: before the sin, the supernal wheat and wine of the Written and Oral Torah were pure spiritual delight, whereas through the Serpent’s seduction physical craving was mingled into them.” Context and connection to Peri Tzadik: In Peri Tzadik, Bereshit 8, Rav Tzadok cites this kabbalistic teaching (Tikkunei Zohar 69a:3-70a:3) to illuminate his exposition here (“And this explains what they taught in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24) and Tikkunei Zohar Chadash: " "The Rabbis said: The tree from which Adam the First ate was wheat; and some Rabbis said: it was a...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the inner dimensions of Torah and divine service developed in Peri Tzadik.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: 2 (§9): For all times are not equal to the heart's Binah whence prayer issues; prayer being the final attribute [Malchus] which is termed "Time" (Et); standing under temporal time, being "a time to act for Hashem," containing the twenty-eight seasons of Ecclesiastes (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 24). In contrast, the Torah transcends time, standing not "under heaven" but above heaven; as the Sages expounded on "under the sun" (Koheles 1:9): the Torah is above the sun; from which issue festivals, days, and cosmic time, having preceded Creation where time began.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 45:1
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: As taught in the Jerusalem Talmud (Pesachim 10:1), slaves eat standing in anxious haste, whereas on Pesach night Israel reclines in royal freedom. Eating is called a spiritual battle—‘bread of war’ (Zohar III:188b)—because physical nourishment can either draw a person down into bodily coarseness or, when eaten in holiness for the sake of Heaven, be elevated into vitality for Torah and divine service.

English_Source_Translation_And_Context: Rosh Hashanah 27a: ‘This, however, is difficult. Come and hear that which was taught in a mishna: If one blew the initial tekia, a long, continuous shofar blast, of the first tekia-terua-tekia set, and then drew out the final tekia of that set so that it spans the length of two tekiot, it counts as only one tekia and is not considered two tekiot, i.e., the final tekia of the first set, and the initial tekia of the second set. But why is this so? Let it count for him as two tekiot, since as stated above, half a blast is considered a blast. The Gemara explains: If one hears only the beginning or the end of a shofar blast, he has indeed fulfilled his obligation, but nevertheless we do not divide a shofar blast…’ Context and connection to Peri Tzadik: In Peri Tzadik, Bereshit 8, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Rosh Hashanah 27a) to illuminate his exposition here (“Just as Rabbenu Tam found difficult regarding the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua on the date of Creation (Rosh Hashanah 27a, Tosafot). However, according to what has been explained,...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the inner dimensions of Torah and divine service developed in Peri Tzadik.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: 1 (§8): The matter is that the future redemption takes place at the time associated with the world’s creation, according to either opinion of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, because then the purpose of Creation will be completed. The beginning of Creation itself came solely through an awakening from Above, from the blessed Hashem, since no awakening from below could yet exist.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 55:10
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: The second utterance corresponds to the letter Hei of the Name Havayah, hinting at Hashem's love for Israel, and infusing holy strength into the heart of Israel; for even if the earned merit of the Patriarchs has ceased, the Covenant of the Patriarchs has not ceased, as brought in the Talmud (Shabbat 55a) and Tosafot there: ancestral merit (zechut avot) points to the power of the Patriarchs' personal spiritual service; while the covenant of the Patriarchs (brit avot) points to what is written “As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you”.
